title: Enforce signed session keys with policy-bound names and audit enrichment
creator: Alex Kim
description: Add enforcement and rollout plan for a new signed-session key format plus audit enrichment pipeline. Goal: reduce blast radius for leaked keys, make revocation safer and faster, and add deterministic, policy-bound naming metadata to every issued session key for observability. This is a cross-cutting change touching auth service (token minting), gateway routing (enforcement), admin console (key listing + filters), and logging pipeline (audit enrichment).
acceptance_criteria: All newly minted session keys adopt the signed-session format (compact signed payload + policy-hash) in prod after feature flag is enabled.
Gateway rejects tokens that do not validate signature or policy-hash when 'strict-signed-session' flag is on.
Admin console displays key attributes (environment, purpose, issuer, policy-id) parsed from the signed payload and allows filtering/search by policy-id.
Audit pipeline enriches token usage logs with policy metadata and stores both raw token fingerprint and policy-id for at least 90 days.

A revocation wave can be triggered by policy-id to invalidate all session keys matching the policy within the SLA defined in the incident playbook (target: 2 minutes for gateway propagation in Dedicated/Hosted).
Performance impact on p50/p95 latency for token validation is <5% for typical requests (validated by load test).
implementation_notes: Design chooses compact JWS-like structure signed with Redwood signing key; payload contains minimal claims: issuer, env, policy_id, created_at, ttl_seconds, nonce.
Policy-id is a stable identifier derived from the RBAC policy blob (sha256 short hex). Do not store secrets in payload.
Gateway will implement a caching validator: signature verification + policy hash check, with hot-key cache for active tokens.
For Dedicated customers, we provide an opt-in key acceptance mode before full enforcement; rollout controlled via feature flag 'strict-signed-session'.

Audit enrichment performed in two stages: (1) gateway attaches token fingerprint + policy-id to the request event, (2) ingestion pipeline joins with policy metadata and indexes fields for Console/UI filters.
Backward compatibility: accept legacy API keys when gateway flag = false. Migration plan documented in links below.

Revocation mechanism: maintain a per-policy revocation list (RList) keyed by policy-id; gateway checks token's policy-id against RList TTL cache. RList updates propagate via streaming notifications (pub/sub).
comments: 2025-02-11 — Alex Kim: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence. Agreed on compact signed format (JWS-like) to avoid introducing heavy crypto libs into gateway. Action: auth-service to prototype signing API.
2025-02-17 — Priya Nair: Implemented initial signing endpoint in auth-service (PR #842). Prototype issues: token size increased by ~38 bytes; raised with infra about header limits on older proxies.
2025-02-20 — Infrastructure (R. Ortega): Confirmed our proxy stack supports header sizes up to 16KB. Suggest placing token in Authorization header as before; no change required.

2025-02-24 — Security review (L. Martin): Requested that policy-id be derived from canonicalized policy JSON to avoid accidental collisions. Also requested threat model for RList to ensure it cannot be used for DoS.

2025-02-28 — Priya Nair: Gateway PR #2210 opened for signature validation and RList check. Added fallback cache for legacy key acceptance. Load tests in staging show p95+8% without hot-key cache; hot-key cache reduces p95 to +2%.
2025-03-03 — Data Engineering (S. Zhao): Audit enrichment pipeline added a join step; indexing policy-id increased ES storage by ~0.6% per month. Confirm retention 90 days is acceptable vs cost.
2025-03-05 — Priya Nair: Feature flag 'strict-signed-session' ready. Plan: Enable in staging 2025-03-09, beta customers 2025-03-13, full enforcement 2025-03-20 pending rollouts and monitor.
Follow-ups: document emergency revoke runbook, add observability alert for RList propagation lag, and add migration script for customer-managed tokens.
